title: Ports
hook: One IP address is a building. Ports are the doors — 80, 443, 22 lead to different services.

steps.caption: Same server IP, but your browser knocks on port 443 for HTTPS.

nodeCaptions.client: The destination is IP + port, not IP alone.
nodeCaptions.p443: A process is listening on 443. Other ports are other programs.

steps.caption: SSH uses 22 on that same machine. Different door, different service.

nodeCaptions.p22: Firewalls often allow 443 but block 22 from the public internet.
nodeCaptions.p80: Port 80 is the classic unencrypted HTTP door.

takeaways: IP finds the host; port finds the service on that host.
Well-known ports are conventions — the OS maps them to listening processes.
Security often means choosing which doors are open.

quiz.question: Two services on one server — how does traffic reach the right one?
choices: Different port numbers on the same IP
They must use different IP addresses always
DNS picks the service name only
quiz.explanation: Sockets are addressed by IP + port (+ protocol).
